text: Thursday evening above Mangwon: Nib sprints across the rooftops, a huge orange cat right behind him.
Through Nib's eyes: all claws, whiskers and yellow eyes.
He leaps a gap between buildings. So does the cat.
At home, Jaeha sits with his eyes shut, linked to Nib. Why is a cat chasing his summon? That's Gomi. She owns the neighbourhood.
It's Link training, and Seoa keeps the numbers: forty metres, ninety, a hundred and sixty. One nosebleed.
Jaeha smiles helplessly. A second one starts.
Then Nib is yanked to a stop like a dog on a leash. Range limit, a hundred and sixty metres.
Seoa holds a tissue to his nose. They agreed to stop at two. One more push. The cat is gaining.
His eyes snap open. Link level three: range up to six hundred metres. But strain above ninety percent causes bleeding.
The leash stretches, and Nib races toward the river, the cat two roofs behind.
He drops into the park by the Han River.
Under a bridge, by a pier marked with a yellow seven: a fence hung with black tarps, a humming generator, and cables running toward a cold glow.
Through Nib's eyes: a gate slit with cables plugged into a steel frame round its rim. No tape, no cones, no sign.
Seoa checks the gate app. Registered gates within a kilometre: zero.
Two guards in black walk past the fence. Jaeha spots it: they all wear the same silver pin, a hexagon inside a hexagon.
Seoa knows it at once: the Kanghan logo. It is on every core battery in Seoul.
One guard swings his torch toward Nib's hiding place.
It lands on Gomi, calmly licking her paw atop the pallets. Just a cat. A very fat cat.
Jaeha writes it all down: a gate nobody registered, under the bridge, with Kanghan guards and cables.
Why would a company hide a gate? He doesn't know yet. But he's writing it down.
Nib staggers home, and Gomi strolls in behind him. She likes him, says Seoa. She wants to eat him, says Nib.
Nib holds the high ground on the water tank. Gomi is in love.
Saturday brings their first gate as a team, and the rent is still due.
D-grade Gate 3318: a car park flooded with black water, and a long dry ramp leading down into it.
Bomi goes live with the Trap Rats. Jaeha reminds her of the rules. Never his face.
Something big moves just under the surface, and a sunken car rocks.
Nib can't fight in that; it's over his head. Then they won't fight in the water.
A drip lands, and a long jaw of crooked teeth snaps at the ripples.
Jaeha flicks a pebble out, and a wake surges toward it from across the car park.
Notebook: blind, it hunts by ripples. Fast in water, clumsy on dry concrete.
The plan: he splashes, it comes, and he leads it up the ramp onto dry ground, under a pipe where Nib will wait.
Yerin grabs his sleeve. He's the bait? Again? He's a trap-tester, he says. Bait is what he's best at.
Nib climbs onto the ceiling pipe above the dry part of the ramp.
And Jaeha walks down alone and splashes at the water's edge.
The drowned hound erupts from the water: horse-sized, weed-covered, pale blind eyes, a crack of violet ash on its brow.
Jaeha runs up the ramp, and the hound comes after him, far faster than it should be.
Its jaws clamp on his left forearm and yank him off his feet.
Yerin screams his name.
And it starts dragging him back down toward the water.
The pain in Jaeha's eyes turns cold. Nib. Now.
On the pipe, Nib's eyes flare amber. Field form, five minutes, linked.
He drops onto the hound's head and drives both knives into the crack. The jaws spring open.
The hound bucks and thrashes on the wet concrete, Nib hanging on by one knife.
Bomi shoots with her eyes squeezed shut. Get away from her co-star! The arrow flies far over the hound.
And hits a parked car. The alarm goes off.
The blind hound whips its head toward the noise, and its brow is wide open.
Nib drives both knives down with his whole weight, and the hound bursts into ash and black water.
Ash and water rain down on the ramp. The car alarm keeps shrieking.
Yerin heals the bite on Jaeha's arm. Good shot, Bomi, he says. She was aiming at its head!
Twelve thousand people are watching. The husk jumped from the ceiling! She shot a car!
A violet core floats up out of the puddle. Boss defeated: Drowned Hound, D-grade.
Then a second window. Harvest the core, an estimated three million won. No other option is available.
Last time there was a release button, Jaeha says. This time, only harvest. Then it was only a beast, says Nib.
But for once, he doesn't look sure.
The core drifts into Jaeha's palm. No release. He'll write that down too.
Operator level three to four, and a second summon slot. Route Alignment starts syncing a new kind of boss.
The core sells for three million, a million each. For once, it's enough.
That night, Seoa hands the landlady the rest of the rent, and next month's too. And the pet?
Seoa doesn't even turn round. He's not a pet, ma'am. He's a husk.
Then pork belly on the rooftop grill with Seoa, Yerin and Bomi, and Gomi watching Nib from the water tank.
Nib holds out a lettuce wrap. You first. Seoa takes a bite. It's lettuce. It's always lettuce.
Seoa's budget: rent paid, next month paid, school trip paid.
Later, alone at the parapet: a gate nobody registered, guarded by the company that sells the cores.
Far away, under the bridge, a faint cold glow.
Then a window. Sync complete. A new kind of boss, ten percent times Operator level four.
Route Alignment, sixty to one hundred percent. The Far Side can hear him now.
His pencil falls from behind his ear.
A huge window with one glowing button. A call is available. Speak, and the Far Side will hear his offer.
The button glows in both his eyes. The Far Side is listening.
